modifications: Establish a separately versioned security-correlation layer over authenticated frozen Alpaca downloads and lineage evidence.
Partition every source row into digest-bound correlated and uncorrelated branch outputs, then publish their receipt last.
Apply explicitly ordered ownership-interval and row-correlation rule registries and record rule provenance in correlation outputs.
Establish an exclusive terminal ticker-ownership boundary from an identity-resolved cash-merger acquiree action.
Establish a base ownership interval when complete corporate-action evidence and the current asset lookup agree on exactly one input-symbol identity.
Apply ticker transitions and terminal merger boundaries as constraints on that base interval while preserving ambiguous ticker reuse as uncorrelated.
Assign every correlated row segment to its exact Alpaca asset UUID and preserve name changes as directed UUID-to-UUID lineage edges without collapsing identity nodes.
Separate UUID attribution from boundary confidence so a unique candidate can pass with explicit warnings, while only missing or tied UUID candidates remain uncorrelated.
Prefer the asof-selected UUID predecessor branch over unrelated ticker reuse and preserve conflicting duplicate merger boundaries as warnings.
Keep mutable asset names and status in the lineage snapshot rather than serializing them as canonical historical identity.
Publish security-correlation branch manifests and their digest-binding receipt inside the owning data/end_of_day symbol directory with all other production pipeline manifests.
Use an asset-resolved same-ticker stock-merger event as a dated transition between distinct predecessor and successor Alpaca UUIDs.
Preserve that transition as a stock-merger UUID lineage edge while excluding unrelated merger inputs from the requested ticker lineage.
Introduce a deterministic SHA-256 internal security identifier derived from the sorted unique Alpaca asset-ID set while retaining exact Alpaca and ticker provenance.

At the final correlation boundary, promote a fully uncorrelated same-ticker history only when exactly two stable Alpaca ID candidates exist and every expected market session is present through the request endpoint.
Retain the two candidates, calendar proof, potential corporate-action explanation, and an unresolved-vendor-boundary warning on every continuity-based promotion.

Bind an explicit symbol disposition to each correlation generation, distinguishing supported assets, retained historical symbol-only series, evidence-backed OTC or inactive-empty out-of-scope assets, quarantined empty symbols, exchange test symbols, and unresolved evidence.
Mark an exact-404 historical alias as just_skip only when one corporate-action/CUSIP occupant resolves to an Alpaca asset ID and all eight authenticated SIP/1Day views are empty.
Keep UUID-less historical and test rows in the exhaustive uncorrelated branch with a deterministic non-security market-data-series ID rather than fabricating an Alpaca or master security identity.
Publish disposition work items and explicit reason codes so recurring orchestration can skip authenticated quarantined or excluded symbols without deleting frozen evidence.
Generalize the terminal continuous-ticker fallback to a stable non-empty set of same-ticker, same-name Alpaca UUID candidates anchored by exactly one current symbol lookup.
Retain and report candidates whose current asset ticker does not match the requested ticker, but exclude them from the promoted security identity.
Continue authenticating version-8 correlation artifacts during targeted version-9 migration so unaffected frozen histories do not require a universe rerun.
Treat a gap of at least 60 expected US market sessions as evidence of possible ticker reuse and partition the symbol history at the last such gap.
Assign only the complete rightmost pricing run to a unique current symbol lookup with a non-empty asset name, preserving every earlier pricing run as uncorrelated.
Prevent the undated unique-UUID fallback from joining histories across a qualifying ticker-reuse gap when the current run cannot be allocated.
Restrict the 60-session ticker-gap assessment to candidate detection because calendar continuity, a current name, and an undated symbol lookup do not establish historical security identity.

Fail closed on both sides of a detected ticker-reuse gap before applying existing interval or candidate fallbacks; a later correlation rule may promote an episode only when it proves complete dated identity evidence for that episode.
Preserve the current lookup only as diagnostic candidate evidence.
Bind authenticated venue-session exclusions to the exact Alpaca UUID, CUSIP, exchange, market calendar, and primary-source bytes used by online availability evaluation.
Resolve a missing-session boundary only when every missing session is inside the verified full-session suspension and no positive-activity raw bar occurs inside it.

Allocate only a complete rightmost pricing suffix after at least 100 missing market sessions when every authenticated adjustment has the identical session set and the current symbol resolves to exactly one UUID, CUSIP, non-empty name, and exchange.
Keep every pre-gap row uncorrelated and veto allocation of both sides when explicit dated lineage evidence assigns a pre-gap session to the current suffix UUID.
Keep the 60-session gap detector and fail-closed guard ahead of all existing identity fallbacks so rejected gaps cannot be joined by an inferred or generic correlation rule.
Allow the complete current suffix to publish without a CUSIP when every other allocation gate passes and the current symbol resolves to one exact Alpaca UUID.
Continue to reject current identities with multiple conflicting CUSIPs.
Allow an otherwise-qualified, internally complete rightmost suffix to publish when its exact Alpaca asset status is inactive, even when the suffix ends before the global request endpoint.

Keep an otherwise-qualified incomplete suffix offline and flag it when the exact Alpaca asset remains active; reject the inactive rule when dated right-suffix evidence identifies a different Alpaca UUID.

Allocate a post-gap rightmost pricing episode to a different Alpaca UUID when an exact CUSIP lookup and unambiguous corporate-action ownership interval identify it and its authenticated session grid is complete through the dated terminal boundary.
Treat a conflicting undated symbol lookup as a recorded warning, keep pre-gap rows uncorrelated, and reject the allocation when explicit dated evidence assigns the same UUID to the pre-gap episode.
Partition a one-session action boundary when the old and new tickers each resolve to one different Alpaca UUID, no third UUID competes for either ticker, and all authenticated adjustment grids agree.
Evaluate the two internally complete pricing episodes as isolated security identities while retaining the corporate-action relationship as provenance.
Keep action-linked Alpaca UUID histories as separate security identities when every UUID has one internally continuous authenticated session run in all eight adjustment views.
Apply the partition after dated row identity resolution so the rule changes grouping without reinterpreting source rows or treating intervening sessions as nontrading.
Reject the partition when any UUID recurs across an internal gap, overlaps another UUID, lacks an adjustment view, or relies on an undated identity assignment.

Assign a complete current ticker run to its exact current Alpaca UUID after authenticated evidence shows the prior occupant renamed away at least 100 market sessions earlier and dated nonstructural actions bind the later ticker and CUSIP to the new UUID.
Keep the historical occupant separate and reject the rule on incomplete adjustment grids, unresolved identity evidence, competing in-run occupancy, or an in-run structural action.
Preserve authenticated predecessor and successor UUID lineage when complete, inactive, or dated terminal ticker-reuse suffix rules assign pricing rows to one proven UUID.
Suppress UUID-lineage edges only for explicit identity partitions, keeping ticker-occupancy allocation separate from security-membership partitioning.

Treat an exact same-symbol forward or reverse split with valid rates, date, distinct old and new CUSIPs, and unique authenticated US-equity endpoint lookups as one security identity across both Alpaca UUIDs.

Retain the split effective date and endpoint CUSIPs as identity provenance without using the split action to promote or reassign pricing rows, and exclude split edges from distinct-security episode partitioning.

Suppress only the corporate-action edges certified by an explicit identity partition so an unrelated identity-preserving split remains connected without pulling a partitioned predecessor into the security.

Resolve overlapping authenticated ownership intervals by selecting the single interval with the most recent explicit start date after stronger as-of lineage evidence and before the requested-symbol fallback.
Fail closed when overlapping claims have no explicit start date or tie for the most recent start, and keep ticker occupancy selection separate from security-identity membership.

Follow the single listed US-equity symbol returned by both exact CUSIP endpoints of a structurally complete name change when those endpoint lookups resolve to the same Alpaca UUID, repeating to a deterministic fixed point and rejecting ambiguous, malformed, placeholder, OTC, and traversal-limit evidence.

Treat overlapping ownership intervals for one identical Alpaca UUID as noncompeting security claims so the existing exact requested-symbol interval rule decides row provenance, while retaining fail-closed overlap handling for different UUIDs.
